explain.say: See the computer? Every beep at the till tells the shop's computer one item has sold. It counts everything and even predicts what people will want, like more ice cream when the forecast is sunny. What would you stock up on before a festival?

faq.q: How does the shop know what to reorder?
faq.a: Every item scanned at the till is counted by the shop's computer. It compares sales with stock, predicts what will be needed, and sends orders automatically.
asks: How do supermarkets know when to restock?

faq.a: A huge warehouse where goods from many suppliers arrive, get sorted, and are packed into mixed loads for each shop.

faq.q: Why are shelves often filled at night?
faq.a: Roads are quieter for lorries and the aisles are empty of shoppers, so workers can restock quickly and safely.

faq.q: How does fresh food stay fresh on the way?
faq.a: Chilled and frozen lorries keep food at the right temperature from warehouse to shop. This unbroken chain of cold is called the cold chain.

faq.q: How do bananas ripen in time?
faq.a: They are picked green, shipped cool, then ripened in warm rooms using ethylene, a natural ripening gas that bananas make themselves.

facts: Bananas are usually picked green and ripened later with ethylene gas in ripening rooms.
The cold chain keeps chilled and frozen food at safe temperatures from producer to shop.
